newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: WOOLDRIDGE DEFENDS HEALTH INSURANCE REBATE
Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, says he's not yet been formally asked by health insurer, Medibank Private, to approve a 15 per cent increase in its hospital cover premium.
Dr Wooldridge says the reported move by Medibank will receive as much scrutiny as the law allows, but he says present legislation makes it hard to refuse such applications.
But he says it's silly to claim premium increases would wipe out the Government's health insurance rebate, which comes into effect in July.
The Minister says the rebates are costing the Government one-point-seven billion dollars, and if they weren't in place, premiums would be even higher.
SURVEY FINDS ONE-THIRD OF EMPLOYERS EXPECT TO HIRE MORE
Almost a third of employers approached in the latest in a series of regular national hiring intention surveys intends to take on new staff in the next three months.
This compares with 15-point-four per cent who intend to shed workers.
The survey results represent the first pick-up in hiring intentions in a year-and-a-half.
Human resources consultant, Morgan and Banks, surveyed 3,200 organisations for the study.
Head of economic research, John Winter, says the net increase is positive for employment, and represents a recognition by employers of sound fundamentals in the economy.
PLAN TO UPGRADE FACILITIES FOR REMOTE ABORIGINALS
Health Minister Michael Wooldridge says it's a national disgrace that Aboriginal Australians still don't have the same services as the rest of the population.

To try to rectify this, a proposal is to be put up for Prime Ministerial approval to deploy military engineers and support staff to build basic infrastructure, like sewerage and water supply, for remote communities.
Dr Wooldridge says Aboriginals have the same right to clean water as other Australians and there's no doubt conditions would improve under the plan.
He says although the Prime Minister has said defence personnel shouldn't be used for non-military projects, this is a special case.
MULTI-MEDIA TRAINING CENTRE OPENS
Federal Employment and Education Minister, Amanda Vanstone, has opened a multi-media training centre in Sydney.
The Access Australia Cooperative Multi-Media centre is designed to conduct research and to supply training to professionals, managers and teachers in the use of multi-media and the World Wide Web.

The Sydney Access facility is part of the Cooperative Multi-media program linked to universities throughout Australia. Senator Vanstone has announced that Australia's six cooperative multi-media centres will receive two million dollars in additional Government funding for research into copyright.
CHILD-CARE REPORT CRITICISED
A taskforce report on the future of the child-care industry is under fire.
The Quality Child-care Association has criticised the report from the Economic Planning Advisory Commission as simplistic and naive.
The Commission recommends scrapping all current funding methods for child-care and replacing them with a single means-tested payment to all parents using child-care.
It says this will provide a level playing field between private and community centres.

The Child-care Association's Executive Member, Dennis Peterson says the changes will provide an incentive for parents to take their children out of formal, high quality care and put them into cheaper, low quality home based care.
QLD PAEDOPHILIA REPORT DUSTED OFF
The Queensland Government has opened the way to revisit the Sturgess Report on paedophilia.
The findings of the Sturgess Report released in 1986, have been largely ignored by Governments and other authorities.
Families, Youth and Community Care Minister, Kev Lingard, says Parliament has agreed to the appointment of an independent
Children's Commissioner, and one of their first tasks will be to re-examine the Sturgess Report findings.
Mr Lingard says that within 12 months the commissioner will report to parliament about paedophilia in Queensland.
He says he'll ask the commissioner to look again at the Sturgess report to assess whether it's relevant to the present time.
BLACKHAWK PILOT HIGHLIGHTS FAULTS
The pilot of one of the Blackhawk helicopters which collided in north Queensland in June says the light created as the other helicopter crashed helped him land his aircraft upright.
Captain David Burke will continue to give evidence at the Blackhawk inquiry in Townsville today.
Captain Burke's crew say they owe their lives to his skill in landing the Blackhawk, after the collision.
Of 15 on board, eight survived, while 10 soldiers on the other Blackhawk died.
Captain Burke told the inquiry a number of factors contributed to the crash.
He said a white board map was wrong, there was no photo of the target area and targets for the counter-terrorism exercise were a trap for night vision goggles, which reduce perception.
RELIGIOUS LEADERS URGE HOUSING POVERTY REFORM
Australia's religious leaders are calling on the Prime Minister and state Premiers to urgently reduce housing-related poverty.
A 10-point national affordable housing strategy has been signed by 16 religious leaders who've written to the Prime Minister and the Premiers, demanding action.
The strategy will be presented at Friday's Council of Australian Government's meeting.
LEGAL ACTION SOUGHT OVER POKIE NON-PAYOUT
Legal action is being sought by a Melbourne pokies player, whose winning cheque was cancelled due to a gaming machine malfunction.
Wayne Smith, who's nineteen years old, walked away with a cheque for A$9,800, after playing a 10-cent "Green Lizard" machine at Preston's Olympic Hotel, on October 17th.
Mr Smith was telephoned later in the day by the hotel manager, who explained the cheque was cancelled because of the malfunction.
Tabcorp owns the machine and the Victorian Casino and Gaming Authority is investigating the matter.
Mr Smith's lawyer, Charles Power, says Tabcorp has witheld information about how gaming disputes are resolved.
Mr Power says Tabcorp refused to supply Mr Power with a copy of the procedures on the grounds they were confidential.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
